## Contract review: `packages/web` ↔ `packages/api/billing`

I read both sides against the scan. The headline: **all four client functions disagree with the backend. Zero of the four would do the right thing against the real route table.** The scan reports 5 findings, but only 4 are contract issues, and it misses 5 more — the ones its own caveat about runtime-assembled URLs predicts it would miss.

Full route table, for reference:

| Client call (`workspace-client.ts`) | Backend declares (`routes.py`) | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces/<id>` :18 | `GET /api/teams/{team_id}` :10 | 404 |
| `POST /api/workspaces` :23 | `POST /api/teams` :15 | 404 |
| `GET /api/teams/:id/seats` :28 | `GET /api/teams/{team_id}/seats` :20 | **200, wrong data** |
| `PUT /api/teams/:id/plan` :34 | `POST /api/teams/{team_id}/plan` :25 | 405, then 422 |

---

### Ranked by how they fail in production

I've ranked by *probability of reaching production × damage once there*, not raw severity. The 404s and the 405 break on the first click of a smoke test and never ship. The silent ones ship.

#### 1. `Plan` enum drift — nothing validates it on either side (HIGH)
`plans.py:10` declares `[free, pro, team, scale]`; `workspace-client.ts:10` declares `[free, pro, enterprise]`. Only `free` and `pro` are shared.

The scan's evidence line says *"only in TypeScript: enterprise — the Python side will reject this value."* **That is wrong for this code.** `change_team_plan` is typed `plan: str` (`routes.py:26`), not `plan: Plan`, and echoes the value back unvalidated. So `"enterprise"` is accepted and persisted as a plan the backend has no concept of. `seats_for` then hits `SEATS_INCLUDED.get(plan, 1)` (`plans.py:29`) and silently returns **1 seat** — a billing-correctness bug with no error anywhere in the stack.

The other direction is equally silent: the backend returns `"team"` or `"scale"`, `res.json()` casts it to `Plan` with no runtime check, and every `switch`/ternary on plan tier falls through its default branch. TypeScript gives you zero protection at a `fetch` boundary.

Fix: generate one side from the other. Also change `plan: str` → `plan: Plan` on line 26 so the backend stops accepting garbage.

#### 2. `:id` is sent as a literal string, never interpolated (HIGH — scan missed this)
`workspace-client.ts:28` and `:34` fetch `"/api/teams/:id/seats"` — Express-style placeholder syntax, inside a template that is never interpolated. Both functions accept an `id` parameter and **never use it**.

This is the worst failure mode in the repo because it doesn't fail. FastAPI's `{team_id}` path segment matches the literal string `:id` happily, so `team_seats` returns **HTTP 200** with `team_id = ":id"`. And because `team_seats` ignores `team_id` entirely and hardcodes `seats_for(Plan.FREE)` (`routes.py:22`), every workspace in the product reports **1 seat**, forever, with a green response. No 4xx, no log line, no alert. You find this from a customer complaining about seat limits.

The two sides disagree on path-parameter syntax itself (`:id` vs `{team_id}`), which is the class of bug a literal-string scanner can't see.

#### 3. No response-status checking anywhere (HIGH — scan missed this)
All four functions call `res.json()` without checking `res.ok`. FastAPI's error responses are valid JSON (`{"detail": "Not Found"}`), so every failure below gets cast to `Workspace` and flows into the UI as `workspace.plan === undefined`.

This is the amplifier that makes items 4–7 dangerous. On its own each is a clean 404/405; combined with this, they surface as "the plan badge is blank" or "undefined is not a valid plan" three components downstream from the actual cause. Fix this first — it converts every remaining item into a legible error.

#### 4. `GET /api/workspaces/<id>` — path not declared (HIGH — scan missed this)
`workspace-client.ts:18` reads `/api/workspaces/` + id; the backend only declares `/api/teams/{team_id}`. 404 on **every workspace read** — the single highest-traffic call in the client.

The scan flagged only the `POST` variant (item 5) and not this one. Its own coverage note explains why: *"matched on literal path strings — a route or URL assembled at runtime is invisible to this check."* The `"/api/workspaces/" + id` concatenation hid it. Worth knowing that this detector systematically under-reports on any client that builds URLs dynamically — which is most of them.

#### 5. `POST /api/workspaces` — path not declared (MEDIUM — scan `crime_00005`)
`workspace-client.ts:23` vs `POST /api/teams` (`routes.py:15`). 404 on workspace creation. Same root cause as #4, same misleading surface.

Separately: `create_team` takes `payload: dict`, but the client sends **no body at all**. Even at the right path, this call sends nothing.

#### 6. `PUT` vs `POST` on `/plan` (MEDIUM — scan `crime_00003`)
`workspace-client.ts:34` uses `PUT`; `routes.py:25` declares `POST`. The scan's read is right and its framing is the useful part: because the path exists, this is a **405, not a 404**, which on-call reliably misreads as an auth or proxy problem.

#### 7. The `plan` argument is never sent (MEDIUM — scan missed this)
`changeWorkspacePlan(id, plan)` accepts a `plan` and sends neither a body nor a query string (`workspace-client.ts:34`). `change_team_plan` declares `plan: str` with no default, which FastAPI treats as a **required query parameter** → 422 Unprocessable Entity.

This one is layered behind #6: fix the method and the call still fails, with a different code. Worth fixing in the same change or the "fix" looks like a regression.

#### 8. `team` vs `workspace` naming (LOW — scan `crime_00004`)
No direct runtime failure, but this is the **root cause of #4 and #5** and the reason they'll recur. Note the inconsistency *within* the client: `workspaceSeats` and `changeWorkspacePlan` already use `/api/teams/...`, while `getWorkspace`/`createWorkspace` use `/api/workspaces/...`. Someone renamed half the surface and stopped. The scan's suggestion of `"organization"` would introduce a third name — pick `team` (what the wire format already uses) and rename the client.

#### 9. `changeWorkspacePlan` has no return type (LOW — not in scan)
Line 33 is the only function without a `Promise<T>` annotation, so it returns `Promise<any>`. Minor, but it means the response shape of the write path is unchecked even in principle.

---

### On the fifth scan finding

`crime_00002` (False Identity, `getWorkspace` "performs side effects") is a **false positive here**. An `async` function named `get*` that wraps a `fetch` GET is the idiomatic name; the detector is pattern-matching `fetch` as a side-effect signal without distinguishing a read from a write. Ignore it. The genuine naming problem in this file is #8, which the scan also found — and rated lower.

### What to actually do

The per-item fixes are all small, but hand-patching eight of them recreates the same setup. The structural fix, in order:

1. Add `res.ok` checks (or one shared `request()` helper) — makes everything else diagnosable.
2. Export an OpenAPI schema from FastAPI and generate the client types and paths from it. That kills #1, #2, #4, #5, #6, #7, and #9 permanently, and makes #8 a rename rather than a drift risk.
3. Type `plan: Plan` instead of `plan: str` on `routes.py:26` so the backend validates its own enum.

There are currently no tests and no shared schema (`crimes.config.json` scans only `.ts`/`.py`; there's no OpenAPI artifact in the repo), which is consistent with every finding showing `test_gap: 1`. A single integration test that exercises all four client functions against the real router would have caught seven of these nine.
